name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +16 partisan lean
Castro is a well-funded incumbent; challenger raised under $50k
Prediction markets price Castro near 95% to win
model.rationale: Castro holds a heavily Democratic San Antonio seat, has a large fundraising edge, and markets price him near certain to win. With no competitive polling or ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or unexpected polling showing a single-digit race would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that leans Democratic by about 16 points. He has raised over half a million dollars and holds a large cash advantage over Republican Edgardo Baez, who has raised under $50,000 and shows no outside support. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Castro's chances around 95 percent.

The fundamentals point firmly to Castro: the district's partisan lean, his incumbency, and his financial edge all favor him. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which keeps the margin estimate somewhat loose, but nothing in the available evidence suggests a competitive race.
